Present
PREZ-unt (adj./n.); pri-ZENT (v.)
adj. / v. / n.
Webster 1828 prints PRES'ENT, adjective (Latin praesens: being in a place; now existing; ready at hand) and PRESENT', verb transitive (to set before a superior; to offer; to give; to lay before a court). The noun is that which is given. This page keeps two longer senses in one spelling: being here/now, and setting a thing or a body before the Lord. Companion pages already treat worship, sacrifice, and gift.

Biblical Definition

Present is one spelling with two honest senses. Stress shifts with the sense. Do not mash them.

1. Being here; now existing; not absent. Present is opposed to absent, past, and future. Jesus says, These things I have spoken to you while being present with you. The disciples had His face then. The church has His Spirit now. 'The present' is not a shrine. It is the hour under God's eye.

2. To set before; to offer. To present is to place before a superior. There was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD. Paul beseeches the brethren to present their bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God. A wrapped gift may be a present. Romans 12 is not Christmas. The dictionary therefore keeps present from becoming a mindfulness brand. You are present before God, or you are only nearby.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828: PRES'ENT, adjective — being in a place; now existing; ready at hand (John 14:25). PRESENT', verb transitive — to set before a superior (Job 1:6); to offer; to give. PRESENT, noun — a gift.

expand to see more

PRES'ENT, adjective s as z. [Latin praesens; prae and sum, esse, to be.]

1. Being in a certain place; opposed to absent.

2. Being before the face or near; being in company. These things have I spoken unto you, being yet present with you. John 14:25.

4. Now existing, or being at this time; not past or future.

PRESENT', verb transitive

1. To set, place or introduce into the presence or before the face of a superior. Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord. Job 1:6.

4. To give; to offer gratuitously for reception.

PRES'ENT, noun That which is presented or given; a gift; a donative.

Key Scripture

Romans 12:1 — "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your reasonable service."

John 14:25 — "These things I have spoken to you while being present with you."

Modern Corruption

Present is corrupted when 'be present' is recast as mindfulness, when the living sacrifice is swapped for a lifestyle gift, and when 'living in the moment' is used to dodge judgment and hope.

expand to see more

The first corruption is the wellness slogan. 'Be present' in the age means notice your breath. John 14:25 is the Son present with His own, speaking words. Attention without the Lord is still absence from Him.

The second corruption is the noun eating the verb. A present is a gift. Romans 12:1 is present your bodies a living sacrifice. That is not a wrapped box and not a brand of generosity. Mercies of God first; then the body on the altar.

The third corruption is the cult of now. Webster's present tense can state what is always true. The age uses 'the present' to refuse both memory of the cross and the coming judgment. The hour is real. It is not a god.

Usage

"Present your bodies a living sacrifice — mercies first, then the altar (Romans 12:1)."

"He spoke these things while being present with you (John 14:25)."

"Keep being-here and setting-before as two senses; a wrapped gift is the noun, not Romans 12."
